Over thirty-five hundred planes were in the sky when America told every flight: stop.
On Friday, the FAA grounded every departing flight across the United States.
Not a storm. Not hackers. Officials say old phone lines and routers got overloaded with data.
For more than four hours, nothing took off. Thousands of flights were cancelled or delayed.
America has done this only twice before: after nine eleven, and in a twenty twenty-three computer outage.
America's sky, stopped not by a storm, but by old wires.
